title: Tenneco Clean Air India Ltd - 544612 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 value-added revenue rose 32.2% YoY to INR15,229 million, but ART-led subsidiary margins compressed on non-indexed commodity costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 34.2% YoY to INR17,183 million and value-added revenue (VAR) grew 32.2% to INR15,229 million, on volume growth of 25.4%. Q2 EBITDA rose 28.7% to INR2,616 million (17.2% of VAR), while Q2 PAT grew 15% to INR1,734 million. H1 PAT growth of 6.2% was flattered by a prior-year one-time interest benefit of about INR254 million net of tax from the Motocare sale. Management attributed margin pressure mainly to non-indexed commodities (lube oil, plastic, rubber) and forex, with recoveries from OEMs still under negotiation.

financial_highlights.change: +6.2% YoY; prior year included ~INR254 million one-time net-of-tax benefit

segments.name: Advanced Ride Technologies (ART)
segments.commentary: Q2 VAR INR8,010 million, up 37.8% YoY; H1 VAR INR15,201 million, up 32.9% YoY. Subsidiary margin fell from about 14% to 11.6% this quarter, attributed to oil-related commodity costs.

segments.name: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 VAR INR7,218 million, up 26.6% YoY; H1 VAR INR13,843 million, up 17.8% YoY. Management cited growth recovery after prior-quarter underperformance.

guidance_outlook: Lifetime order book about INR165,000 million at end-H1, stated as more than 100% coverage of FY2030 revenue target; management said FY2030 revenue is now fully covered, up from 80-90% coverage for FY2028 previously.
Export order book INR8,750 million, providing about 50% coverage of target FY2030 export revenue.
FY27 capex guidance INR350-450 crore; about INR120 crore invested as of September end, management said it is on track.

Three new plants: Clean Air North India (SOP around March 2027, roughly 10% capacity increase), ART suspension West India (SOP around July 2027), Clean Air West India (SOP around September 2027, 12-14% hot-end capacity increase).
Suspension capacity addition of about 1 million shock absorbers by July 2027 and a further 1 million in FY28, per the May announcement.
Dividend: policy exists, but timing and amount not decided; capital prioritised for growth investment first.
Management expects a temporary export slowdown to recover if US tariffs and Middle East oil and freight pressures ease.
capex_capacity: Clean Air hot-end capacity about 2 million units; hot-end lines running at about 99% utilisation per analyst question, with new West India plant adding about 300K hot-end systems.
New West India Clean Air plant investment about INR450 million (Q2 announcement); management cited asset turnover of 3-4x gross block.
Shock absorber base capacity about 19 million units; 2 million additional planned across FY27-FY28.
Management cited ROCE of 94% for FY26 and fixed asset turnover upwards of 8-9x, aided by buying depreciated assets from European and US sister divisions.
demand_pricing: Crisil-cited market share in commercial truck clean air rose to 59% in H1 FY27 from 58% in FY26 and 57% in FY25; ART passenger vehicle shock absorber and strut share about 55%, up from 48% about 18 months earlier.

Export share of order book fell to about 5-6% (INR800-900 crore of about INR15,000 crore) versus 14-20% cited at FY26 end, per analyst; management attributed this to softer Western OEM demand, US tariff uncertainty, freight and oil costs, and delayed or cancelled SOPs.
Exports about 7% of revenue in Q2 FY27.
Clean Air ex-Maruti industry volume grew about 13.3% vs Tenneco clean air volume growth of 18-plus% in the same frame; Maruti business not yet served, targeted for 2029.
Three-wheeler suspension win with an Indo-Korean JV; DaVinci production started on three-door Thar; two next-generation Japanese PV model wins mixing conventional and DaVinci.

Commodity pressure: management said steel is index-linked with a quarter-lag recovery, while lube oil, plastic, rubber and forex are non-index and under negotiation; no recovery booked in P&L until OEM confirmation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ART subsidiary margin drop from about 14% to 11.6% is commodity pass-through lag, and when does it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Middle East-driven commodity inflation. Steel recovers with about a quarter lag, but lube oil, plastic and rubber are non-index; part has been recovered and talks are ongoing, with no timeline committed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the export share of the order book fall versus FY26 levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited softer Western OEM demand, US tariff uncertainty, freight and oil costs, and SOP delays or cancellations; it said the domestic order book grew far faster, diluting the export ratio, and expects recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the content per vehicle and timing for three-wheeler suspension?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will start conventional and move to DaVinci over time; customer name and product not yet disclosed, and specific content per vehicle and production timing were not given.

qa_highlights.question: Will clean air mix shift towards cold end while hot-end capacity is at 99% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no bottleneck is expected; hot-end is higher margin, and a new West India plant adds about 300K hot-end systems on a base of about 2 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why is suspension EBITDA growth only about 10% in H1 despite revenue growth above 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins should rise as DaVinci and semi-active mix grows; the current drag is oil commodity costs, which are not yet recovered from OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and export revenue for H1?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex guidance INR350-450 crore, about INR120 crore spent by September end. Exports about 7% of Q2 revenue; H1 export figure not separately stated.

risks_watch: Non-indexed commodity recovery (lube oil, plastic, rubber, forex) from OEMs remains unresolved; timing not committed.
Export order book weakness, with SOP delays and cancellations tied to US tariffs, Middle East conflict, and freight costs.
Concentration of growth in domestic orders and new plant ramp timing (March, July, September 2027).
Clean Air North India SOP timing; hot-end lines at about 99% utilisation until new capacity is commissioned.
Minimum wage increases in a couple of states and premium freight, plus listed-company costs, weigh on margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, order book and market share, but noticeably defensive on export order decline and cautious on commodity recovery timing, which management declined to commit to.
key_quotes: Optically, it looks low, but I think if you look at the grand scheme of things over time, knowing that Tenneco India has such a strong labor cost advantage and also because of technology equalization, right?
Difficult to commit a timeline for that, but yes, I mean, we will keep on having these discussions with our customer.
So it is largely on account of the geopolitical impact on the prices.
We are growing market share through Tata, through Volvo Eicher, through Ashok Leyland, et cetera, right?

adds.what: Clean Air North India plant (roughly 10% capacity increase)
ART suspension West India plant (shock absorbers)
Clean Air West India plant (12-14% hot-end capacity increase; ~300K hot-end systems; investment about INR450 million)
Suspension capacity addition of about 1 million shock absorbers by July 2027 and a further 1 million in FY28

growth.why: Q2 revenue +34.2% and VAR +32.2% on 25.4% volume growth, with hot-end lines at 99% utilisation and three plants plus shock-absorber additions due between Q4 FY27 and FY28; FY27 capex of INR350-450 crore is on track with about INR120 crore spent, and the lifetime order book (~INR165,000 million) is said to cover FY2030 revenue, though export orders are shrinking to about 5-6% of the order book.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: ART subsidiary margin fell from about 14% to 11.6% on non-indexed lube oil, plastic and rubber costs; recovery is under OEM negotiation with no timeline committed, while DaVinci and semi-active mix is expected to lift suspension margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Clean Air North India (~10% capacity) SOP around March 2027, ART suspension West India SOP around July 2027, Clean Air West India (12-14% hot-end increase, ~300K systems, ~INR450 million) SOP around September 2027, and 1 million shock absorbers by July 2027 are all under construction or approved.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew 25.4% and hot-end lines run at 99% utilisation, with new plants adding capacity; but export share of order book fell to about 5-6% from 14-20%, which is a drag.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Hot-end utilisation at 99% and FY27 capex of INR350-450 crore with about INR120 crore spent; the 2 million shock-absorber addition across FY27-FY28 and the 1 million in FY28 point to further capex, though the FY28 plan is not sized in the brief.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 34.2% and VAR 32.2%, and the lifetime order book (~INR165,000 million) covers FY2030 revenue, but margin pressure from commodities and the export slowdown offset that momentum.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export orders fell to about 5-6% of the order book from 14-20%, commodity recovery is uncommitted, and minimum wage and freight costs weigh on margins; management expects exports to recover only if US tariffs and Middle East pressures ease.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DaVinci production has started on the three-door Thar, two next-generation Japanese PV model wins mix conventional and DaVinci, and a three-wheeler suspension win is in place, though the product and content per vehicle are not yet disclosed.

rows.label: Lifetime order book covers FY2030 revenue
rows.why: Lifetime order book of about INR165,000 million at end-H1 is stated as more than 100% coverage of FY2030 revenue, up from 80-90% coverage for FY2028 previously.

rows.label: Non-indexed commodity recovery from OEMs
rows.why: Part of the lube oil, plastic and rubber cost has been recovered and talks are ongoing, but no recovery is booked until OEM confirmation, and ART margin fell to 11.6% from about 14%.

rows.label: Maruti business entry
rows.why: Maruti business is not yet served and is targeted for 2029, outside the 2-4 quarter window.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, order book and market share (commercial truck share 59%, ART PV share about 55%) but defensive on the export order decline and noncommittal on commodity recovery timing; analysts pressed on export share, margins and hot-end utilisation.
